title: SRE shift scrapbook — July 15 2026
content:
Purpose: informal notes from the SRE shifts this week (incidents, SLO status, handoff bullets, quick runbook edits). Treat as a working scratchpad — will extract items into INF tickets and a formal postmortem where needed.

Summary bullets:
- Week snapshot: two visible incidents that touched production latency and embeddings memory (see below). Error budget for hosted-api write route is down to ~12% for the 30d window.
- SLOs: hosted-api generation availability target 99.9% (30d). Current 30d rolling: 99.88% (consuming ~0.12% -> error budget ~12% left). P95 latency trending up after 07-13 deploy.
- On-call handoffs: added small checklist item to always re-run smoke test against canary after autoscaler config changes.

Incidents
1) Incident: API latency spike (2026-07-13 03:22–04:05 UTC)
- Symptom: sustained P95 climb from ~180ms -> ~420ms; P99 up to 1.1s. Elevated tail latency seen across gen-text endpoints in us-west-2.
- Detection: automated latency SLO alert + customer page about degraded interactive experience.
- What we did: rolled back a recently-promoted autoscaler tuning change (PR #482) at 03:40 UTC; temporarily increased min-instances for dedicated pools; enabled fallback routing to smaller-sequence model variant for flagged tenants.
- Root cause (preliminary): autoscaler race where concurrent scale-down + large warmup batches caused GPU stalls; kernel selection path produced a suboptimal codepath under specific batch size transitions. Regression introduced by infra PR that optimized scaling thresholds.
- Immediate mitigation: rollback + conservative min-instance floor + temporary canary traffic split (10%) to new tuning.
- Follow-ups (create INF-2345): add gating to autoscaler changes (smoke + latency canary), add synthetic test that exercises scale down/up transitions with variable batch sizes, and add telemetry to detect kernel-selection path flips.
- Owner: Miguel T. (on-call lead) + infra eng.

2) Incident: embeddings-worker OOM (2026-07-14 11:10–12:30 UTC)
- Symptom: embeddings pool nodes OOM killed after a model-library upgrade; manifested as failed embed requests for ~30% of requests and increased 5xx.
- Detection: CPU/memory alerts from cluster monitor and an increase in 5xx rate for embedding-route.
- What we did: reverted the library upgrade, scaled up node count temporarily, tuned per-request memory cap, kicked a rolling redeploy to force clean memory state.
- Root cause: change in third-party tokenizer library that kept large VM-side buffers live across requests in a specific codepath.
- Immediate mitigation: pinned library to previous version, added ephemeral buffer free in wrapper, and added memory pressure alarm to embeddings service (threshold lowered).
- Follow-ups: add unit test for buffer lifecycle, more aggressive memory limits in resource quota, postmortem to vendor. Owner: Ana R.

Operational notes / metrics
- Current SLO numbers (approx):
  - hosted-api gen availability (30d): 99.88%
  - embedding-route availability (30d): 99.95%
  - P95 gen latency (last 24h): ~220ms
  - P99 gen latency (last 24h): ~890ms
- Alert noise: The autoscaler alert (scale-flapping) fired 18x this week; ~60% of these were related to noisy traffic from one internal test harness. Action: add a denylist for internal harness IPs and a synthetic harness to exercise scale behavior in a controlled window.

On-call handoff notes (added to checklist)
- Required for every handoff:
  - confirm there are no active incidents with P1/P2 status
  - check error budget dashboard and mention any SLOs under 90% of remaining budget
  - verify last deploys (canary success, PR numbers) and note if any infra PRs are pending that affect autoscaling or memory configs
  - re-run p95 smoke test against canary model variant (script: infra/smoketests/canary_p95.sh)
  - confirm runbook contact list (Pager duty + escalation pager)
- This week's specific handoff: Priya -> Luke (2026-07-15 08:00 UTC). Notable: leave note about embeddings pinned versions and the autoscaler rollback; Luke to watch embedding memory alarms for next 24h.

Runbook edits made (quick)
- autoscaler-runbook.md: added section "scale down race" with checklist to verify kernel-selection telemetry; added link to PR template that forces synthetic canary when autoscaler thresholds change.
- embeddings-runbook.md: added memory cap knobs and pointer to vendor issue tracker.

Outstanding action items (short list)
- [ ] INF-2345: formal postmortem for autoscaler latency regression (owner: Miguel)
- [ ] INF-2351: add synthetic scale flip test (owner: infra-qe)
- [ ] INF-2352: add memory lifecycle unit test for tokenizer wrapper (owner: embeddings team)
- [ ] Run a 4h soak with new autoscaler thresholds in staging and collect tail-latency histograms (owner: release-eng)

Communication / customers
- Sent a short status note to #cust-ops and account owners for tenants who saw degraded latency (07-13 05:00 UTC). No outages classified as P1 customer-impact (per SLA classification).

Random notes / lessons learned (informal)
- Autoscaler changes that look benign at aggregate QPS can still produce tiny per-request path changes that amplify tail latency — need better microbenchmarks that emulate bursty, mixed-length sequences.
- We should consider a short-lived "warmup penalty" metric: track requests that hit GPU warmup and count their contribution to tail latency.

References / links
- INF-2345 (autoscaler postmortem ticket)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 (reverted autoscaler tunings)
- Slack: #sre-ops thread "autoscaler-latency-jul13"
- Confluence draft: confluence://sre/postmortems/2026-07-autoscaler-latency

Notes to self
- Move the handoff checklist into a tiny Google Doc that can be attached to the on-call rota so incidents that happen during OOO are less noisy.
- Re-run the batch of synthetic canary tests against the latest kernel selection binaries and store the histograms in perf-bucket.

End of notes.
